source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Proteus pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL Neptune-system ephemeris and IAU/WGCCRE rotation; the Stooke source origin and west-positive longitude are preserved.
provenance.qualification: Computed Proteus Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: Voyager 2 clear-filter imagery registered to the PDS Stooke shape. Measured sky-background subtraction and bounded illumination correction reduce photographed shading. Gray grid marks unavailable or unreliable samples. The distant hemisphere and cast shadows are not reconstructed. Fine grain is largely source-image noise and must not be interpreted as resolved terrain.
controls.title: Clear-filter mosaic
controls.summary: Brightness is corrected for illumination; much of the fine grain is image noise. The gray grid marks unavailable samples.

controls.label: Filter color
controls.description: Voyager green, blue and violet filters are displayed as red, green and blue. Only their common reliable interior is mapped; the gray grid marks unknown samples. Blur and registration uncertainty limit interpretation to broad patterns at roughly 40 km or coarser near the image centre. Small colored details can be image noise or registration error. This is not true color or a calibrated albedo map.
controls.summary: Three Voyager filters, shown as RGB. Broad color only; gray grid marks unknown coverage.
controls.title: Voyager green / blue / violet filter color

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Radial height above a 208 km reference sphere from Stooke’s Voyager-derived shape model. Shows the broad irregular shape, not local height above a geoid. The archived 5° radius grid includes modeled unseen terrain and can exaggerate facets or depressions. Small craters are not resolved.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
controls.summary: Height relative to a 208 km sphere, from a Voyager shape model. Unseen terrain is modeled; small features are uncertain.
